Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Customers should also be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Add this with
Action Mailbox. Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`,
default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`.

Use Action Mailbox's relay ingress at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated
with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. In test, process incoming mail before the request completes
so a separate worker isn't needed.

Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message.

Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses.
Reuse an existing customer, or create one and send a verification email so they can later use the portal.
Receiving email shouldn't verify their account.

When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each
ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to
the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved
tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket.

Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry.
Ignore automated/list mail.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Helpdesk API

Rails API-only backend for a helpdesk SaaS. The frontend is a separate app and
talks to this service over JSON under `/api/v1`.

## Setup

```sh
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql"
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails server -p 3000        # Puma
```

Tests use their own database. Point `DATABASE_URL` at it for the test run:

```sh
DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_test?host=/var/lib/postgresql" RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:create db:schema:load
DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_test?host=/var/lib/postgresql" bin/rails test
```

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none | PostgreSQL connection |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Base of verification, reset and invitation links, and the only CORS origin allowed |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for all email |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | — | Production SMTP. `SMTP_ADDRESS` is required, so production fails to boot without it |
| `SECRET_KEY_BASE` | — | Required in production by Rails 8, even though the API uses no cookies |

In development, mail is written to `tmp/mails/`.

Mail is sent through Active Job. The default `async` adapter runs jobs inside the web
process and loses queued mail if the process restarts. Configure a persistent queue
adapter before going live.

## Conventions

- Every request is JSON. Successful responses are the resource objects. Errors look like
  `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...}}}`.
- `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>` selects the business. Sign-in, email verification,
  password reset requests and `GET /portal` require it. Signed-in endpoints accept it
  and reject a token used with a different business (`403 wrong_account`).
- Signed-in endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Body |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/account/create` | none | `{"account":{"name","subdomain","admin":{"name","email","password"}}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions` | header | `{"session":{"email","password"}}` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/session` | bearer | — |
| GET | `/api/v1/me` | bearer | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/me` | bearer | `{"user":{"name"}}` |
| PUT | `/api/v1/me/password` | bearer | `{"password_change":{"current_password","password"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/email_verifications` | header | `{"email_verification":{"email"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` | none | `{"email_verification":{"token"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/password_resets` | header | `{"password_reset":{"email"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/password_resets/confirm` | none | `{"password_reset":{"token","password"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/portal` | header | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/registrations` | header | `{"user":{"name","email","password"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/invitation_previews` | none | `{"invitation_preview":{"token"}}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/invitation_acceptances` | none | `{"invitation_acceptance":{"token","name","password"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/invitations` | bearer, admin | — (paginated, `?status=pending\|accepted\|revoked\|expired`) |
| POST | `/api/v1/invitations` | bearer, admin | `{"invitation":{"email","role":"admin\|agent"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/invitations/:id` | bearer, admin | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/invitations/:id/resend` | bearer, admin | — |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/invitations/:id` | bearer, admin | — |
| GET | `/api/v1/users` | bearer, admin | — (paginated, `?role=`, `?suspended=true\|false`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/:id` | bearer, admin | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/users/:id` | bearer, admin | `{"user":{"suspended":true\|false}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/staff` | bearer, staff | — (paginated) |
| GET | `/api/v1/requests` | bearer | — (paginated, `?status=open\|pending\|solved`) |
| POST | `/api/v1/requests` | bearer | `{"request":{"subject","comment":{"body"}}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/requests/:id` | bearer | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/requests/:id` | bearer | `{"request":{"comment":{"body"},"status":"solved"}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/requests/:id/comments` | bearer | — (paginated) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tickets` | bearer, staff | — (paginated, `?status=`, `?assignee_id=12\|unassigned`, `?requester_id=12`, `?priority=normal\|high`, `?q=text`, combinable) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tickets/:id` | bearer, staff | — |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/tickets/:id` | bearer, staff | `{"ticket":{"comment":{"body","public"},"status":"open\|pending\|solved","priority":"normal\|high","assignee_id":12\|null}}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/tickets/:id/comments` | bearer, staff | — (paginated) |
| GET | `/api/v1/account` | bearer | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/account/cancel` | bearer, owner | — |
| POST | `/api/v1/account/reactivate` | bearer, owner | — |

Emailed links point at the frontend:

- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?account=ACME&token=TOKEN`
- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?account=ACME&token=TOKEN`
- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/accept-invitation?",
  "output_tail": "e. Registration is refused for a cancelled business.
- Owners must verify their email before they can sign in.
- Changing a password, or completing a password reset, signs out every session.
- **Cancelling** revokes every session in the business and blocks ordinary access. Only
  the owner can still sign in, and only to reactivate or view the account. Reactivation
  is allowed for 90 days after cancellation.
- Accounts still cancelled after 90 days are permanently deleted, with their users and
  sessions, by:

  ```sh
  bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
  ```

  Schedule this daily (cron, a scheduler, or a job runner).

## Invitations

Admins add people by invitation. Only admins and agents can be invited, and an invitee
joins with the invited role.

- `POST /api/v1/invitations` returns the `invitation` and emails the invitee a link to
  `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/accept-invitation?account=ACME&token=TOKEN`. The token is only in
  that email, never in the API.
- An invitation has `id`, `email`, `role`, `status`, `expires_at`, `accepted_at`,
  `revoked_at`, `invited_by` (`{id, name}`), `created_at` and `updated_at`.
- **Status** is `pending`, `accepted`, `revoked` or `expired`. Accepted and revoked win
  over expired. Pending invitations expire 7 days after they were last sent.
- **One open invitation per email.** An invitation is refused while the email belongs to a
  member, or while another invitation for it is pending (`validation_failed`, with the
  reason under `details.email`). Expired and revoked invitations do not block a new one.
- **Customer registration** is refused for an email with a pending invitation. The message
  is worded so it does not reveal the invitation.
- `POST /invitations/:id/resend` sends a new link that replaces the old one and runs for a
  full lifetime. It works for pending and expired invitations. Accepted and revoked
  invitations cannot be resent (`invitation_accepted`, `invitation_revoked`).
- `DELETE /invitations/:id` revokes the invitation so its link stops working. The record
  stays, as `revoked`. Pending and expired invitations can be revoked. Accepted ones cannot,
  and an invitation cannot be revoked twice.
- `GET /invitations` lists oldest first, filtered with `?status=`. `GET /invitations/:id`
  shows one. Both are admin-only.
- **Acceptance** has two steps, with no sign-in. `POST /invitation_previews` returns
  `invitation_preview` with `email`, `role`, `business_name`, `subdomain` and `expires_at`.
  `POST /invitation_acceptances` with a `name` and `password` creates the user with the
  invited role and a verified email, so the invitee signs in without another verification
  email. It returns `user` and `account` (`201`). A link works once. A failed attempt (for
  example, a short password) leaves the invitation pending.
- An unknown or mismatched token is `invalid_token`. Accepted, revoked and expired
  invitations return `invitation_accepted`, `invitation_revoked` and `invitation_expired`.
  Cancelled businesses return `403 account_cancelled`.

## People

Only admins manage people. Agents and customers get `403`.

- `GET /users` lists everyone in the business, oldest first. Filter with
  `?role=admin|agent|customer` and `?suspended=true|false`. `GET /users/:id` shows one user.
  Users include `suspended`.
- `PATCH /users/:id` with `{"user":{"suspended":true}}` suspends a user, and
  `{"user":{"suspended":false}}` restores them. `suspended` is required (`422` without it),
  and other fields in the body are ignored. Changing a user's role is not supported yet.
- **Suspending** signs the user out everywhere, so their bearer tokens stop working. They
  cannot sign in (`403 user_suspended`). Tickets assigned to them become unassigned. Their
  request's `updated_at` does not change, since that is internal activity.
- **Restoring** lets the user sign in again. Their old sessions are not restored.
- **The last active admin** cannot be suspended (`422 last_active_admin`). Suspended admins do
  not count as active.
- `GET /staff` lists the active admins and agents, oldest first, as `{id, name, role}`. Staff
  use it for assignment controls. Agents and admins can both call it.

## Requests and tickets

Customers work with **requests**, at `/api/v1/requests`. Staff work with the same records as
**tickets**, at `/api/v1/tickets`. Customers can only see their own requests. Staff can see
every request in their business. Another business's records always look missing (`404`).

- A new request is `open`. Its first comment comes with the request.
- Responses return records under `request` or `ticket`, and lists under the plural name
  (`requests`, `tickets`, `comments`). A request has `id`, `subject`, `status`,
  `requester_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at`. A ticket also has the requester as
  `{id, name, email}`.
- A comment has `id`, `body`, `public`, `author` (`{id, name}`) and `created_at`.
  Customers only see public comments. Comments are listed oldest first.
- A ticket also has `priority` (`normal` or `high`), `assignee_id` and `assignee` (`{id, name}`,
  or `null` when unassigned). Customers never see the priority or the assignee.
- **Customer replies** `PATCH /requests/:id` with an optional `comment` and an optional
  `status`. A customer can only set `status` to `solved`. A reply reopens a `pending` or
  `solved` request, unless the same update marks it solved. Sending neither a comment nor a
  status is a `422`.
- **Staff replies** `PATCH /tickets/:id` with an optional `comment`, an optional `status`
  (`open`, `pending` or `solved`), an optional `priority` and an optional `assignee_id`. A reply
  on its own does not change the status. Sending none of them is a `422`.
- **Priority**: a new request is `normal`. `{"ticket":{"priority":"high"}}` marks it `high`, and
  `"normal"` puts it back. Any other value, including `null`, is a `422` (`validation_failed`,
  with the reason under `details.priority`), and nothing else in that update is saved. Customers
  cannot set priority, and a customer's request never shows it. A priority change leaves
  `updated_at` alone, so it does not move the request in the customer's list.
- **Assignment**: `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":12}}` assigns the ticket to a user, and
  `{"ticket":{"assignee_id":null}}` clears it. The assignee must be an active admin or agent
  in the same business (`422` otherwise). Use an ID from `GET /staff`.
- **Private notes**: `{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Checking with billing.","public":false}}}`.
  Customers never see a private note. It leaves the request as the customer sees it, so
  `updated_at`, the status and the position in the customer's list are unchanged. Assignment
  changes are internal in the same way. Only public replies and status changes count as
  customer-visible activity.
- Replies do not send email yet.

Lists are paginated with `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, at most 100). They
return `count`, `page`, `per_page`, `next_page` and `previous_page` next to the records. A
`page` or `per_page` that is not a whole number of 1 or more returns `400 invalid_pagination`.
Requests and tickets are ordered by recent activity, so the request or ticket with the newest
public reply or status change comes first. Users, invitations and staff are ordered by ID,
oldest first. An unknown filter value, such as `?status=lost`, returns `400 invalid_filter`.

**Filtering.** Staff filter `GET /tickets` with any combination of these. Every filter that is
sent must match, so `?status=open&priority=high` returns only open, high-priority tickets.

- `status` is `open`, `pending` or `solved`.
- `assignee_id` is a user ID, or `unassigned` for tickets nobody is working. Use an ID from
  `GET /staff`.
- `requester_id` is a user ID. Use the `id` of a customer.
- `priority` is `normal` or `high`. Values are case-sensitive.
- `q` is a case-insensitive search through subjects and **public** comments. Private notes are
  never searched. The text is literal: `%`, `_` and `\` match themselves, and nothing is treated
  as a pattern or as query syntax. `?q=100%` only matches text that contains `100%`.

A blank value, such as `?status=`, counts as not sent. A malformed value returns
`400 invalid_filter` and names the parameter. That covers an unknown status or priority, an
`assignee_id` or `requester_id` that is not a whole number (`12abc`, `1.5`, `0`), an
`assignee_id` other than a user ID or `unassigned`, a `requester_id` of `unassigned`, and a `q`
that is not a single piece of text or contains a NUL byte.

Customers filter their own `GET /requests` by `status` only. Asking for `priority`, `assignee_id`,
`requester_id` or `q` returns `400 invalid_filter`, rather than a list that looks filtered but is
not.



## Accounts and roles

- Roles are `admin`, `agent` and `customer`. Staff are admins and agents.
  - **Admins** manage people (invitations, users, suspension) and work tickets.
  - **Agents** work tickets.
  - **Customers** use the portal and see only their own requests.
- The admin who registers a business is its **owner**. Only the owner can cancel or
  reactivate the account, and only the owner can sign in to a cancelled account. Other
  admins are invited, so they are not owners.
- Customers register through `POST /api/v1/registrations` with the business header. They
  always get the `customer` role, and use the same verification, sign-in, profile and
  password flows as everyone else. Registration is refused for a cancelled business.
- Owners must verify their email before they can sign in.
- Changing a password, or completing a password reset, signs out every session.
- **Cancelling** revokes every session in the business and blocks ordinary access. Only
  the owner can still sign in, and only to reactivate or view the account. Reactivation
  is allowed for 90 days after cancellation.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  ADMIN = "admin".freeze
  AGENT = "agent".freeze
  CUSTOMER = "customer".freeze
  ROLES = [ADMIN, AGENT, CUSTOMER].freeze
  # Staff work the helpdesk. Customers only see their own requests.
  STAFF_ROLES = [ADMIN, AGENT].freeze
  MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8

  belongs_to :account
  has_secure_password
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :user_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :requests, foreign_key: :requester_id, inverse_of: :requester, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :comments, foreign_key: :author_id, inverse_of: :author, dependent: :destroy

  scope :active, -> { where(suspended: false) }
  scope :staff, -> { where(role: STAFF_ROLES) }

  validates :email,

  validates :password, length: { minimum: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH }, allow_nil: true

  # sign-in takes about as long as a real one and timing does not reveal registered emails.
  def self.burn_password_check(password)

    @placeholder_digest.is_password?(password)

  def admin?
    role == ADMIN
  end

  def owner?
    account.owner_id == id
  end

  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  # Suspends the user. Their sessions end, and tickets assigned to them become unassigned.
  # The last active admin cannot be suspended, so a business always keeps one admin.
  def suspend!
    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      next if suspended?

      if admin? && account.users.active.where(role: ADMIN).where.not(id: id).none?

  end

  def change_password!(new_password)

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# A customer's request for help. Customers see it as a request; staff see the same
# record as a ticket.
class Request < ApplicationRecord
  OPEN = "open".freeze
  PENDING = "pending".freeze
  SOLVED = "solved".freeze
  STATUSES = [OPEN, PENDING, SOLVED].freeze
  NORMAL = "normal".freeze
  HIGH = "high".freeze
  PRIORITIES = [NORMAL, HIGH].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255
  # Default for a keyword that was not sent, so an explicit nil can clear the assignee.
  NOT_GIVEN = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requests
  # The staff member working the ticket. Customers never see it.
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, -> { oldest_first }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :request

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH }
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_active_staff, if: :assignee_id_changed?

  # Replies and status changes touch the request, so this orders by the latest activity.
  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Requests whose subject or public comments contain the text, ignoring case. The text is
  # literal: % and _ match themselves, not wildcards. Private notes are not searched.
  scope :search, lambda { |text|
    pattern = "%#{Request.sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern: pattern)
      requests.subject ILIKE :pattern
      OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.request_id = requests.id
          AND comments.public = TRUE
          AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  }

  # Opens a request with its first comment, from the requester. Both or neither are saved.
  def self.submit!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    transaction do
      request = create!(account: requester.account, requester: requester, subject: subject, status: OPEN)
      request.comments.create!(author: requester, body: body, public: true)
      request
    end
  end

  # A reply from the requester: an optional comment and an optional status.
  #
  # Requesters can only mark a request solved. A comment reopens a pending or solved
  # request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  def requester_reply!(author:, body: nil, status: nil)
    invalid!(:base, "Send a comment, a status, or both.") if body.nil? && status.nil?
    invalid!(:status, "can only be set to solved by the requester") if status && status != SOLVED

    with_lock do
      comments.create!(author: author, body: body, public: true) unless body.nil?

      # `status` here is the argument, so the current value is read through self.
      if status == SOLVED
        self.status = SOLVED
      elsif body && self.status != OPEN
        self.status = OPEN
      end
      save!
    end
  end

  # A reply from staff: an optional comment, an optional status, an optional priority and an
  # optional assignee (a user ID, or nil to unassign). A reply on its own does not change the
  # status.
  #
  # Only a status change is customer-visible here. Public comments touch the request on
  # their own. Private notes, priority and assignments leave updated_at alone, so they are
  # invisible to the customer.
  def staff_reply!(author:, body: nil, public: true, status: nil, priority: nil, assignee_id: NOT_GIVEN)
    assigning = !assignee_id.equal?(NOT_GIVEN)
    if body.nil? && status.nil? && priority.nil? && !assigning
      invalid!(:base, "Send a comment, a status, a priority, or an assignee.")
    end

    # Assigning checks that the assignee is not suspended. Suspension holds the business lock,
    # so take it here too, in the same order. Then a suspension cannot slip in between the
    # check and the save and leave a suspended person assigned.
    if assigning && !assignee_id.nil?
      account.with_lock { apply_staff_reply!(author, body, public, status, priority, assignee_id) }
    else
      apply_staff_reply!(author, body, public, status, priority, assignee_id)
    end
  end

  # The customer's view of a request. Priority is internal, so it is not included.
  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  # The staff view of a request: the same fields, with the requester's details, the priority
  # and the assignee, if any.
  def as_ticket_api_json
    as_api_json.merge(
      requester: { id: requester.id, name: requester.name, email: requester.email },
      priority: priority,
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee && { id: assignee.id, name: assignee.name }
    )
  end

  private

  def invalid!(attribute, message)
    errors.add(attribute, message)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
  end

  def apply_staff_reply!(author, body, public, status, priority, assignee_id)
    assigning = !assignee_id.equal?(NOT_GIVEN)

    with_lock do
      comments.create!(author: author, body: body, public: public) unless body.nil?
      self.assignee_id = assignee_id if assigning
      self.priority = priority unless priority.nil?
      self.status = status unless status.nil?
      save!(touch: status_changed?)
    end
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return if requester.nil?

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same business") unless requester.account_id == account_id
  end

  # Tickets go to working staff only: agents or admins in this business who are not suspended.
  def assignee_is_active_staff
    return if assignee_id.nil?
    return if assignee && assignee.account_id == account_id && assignee.staff? && !assignee.suspended?

    errors.add(:assignee, "must be an active agent or admin in this business")
  end
end

  # A cancelled account can be reactivated for this long. After that it is purged.
  CANCELLATION_WINDOW = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[api app admin www mail].freeze

  StateError = ::StateError

  # The admin who registered the business. Only the owner can cancel or reactivate it.
  belongs_to :owner, class_name: "User", optional: true

  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :requests, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 120 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            length: { maximum: 63 },
            format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens" },
            uniqueness: true
  validate :subdomain_not_reserved

  scope :cancelled_before, ->(time) { where(cancelled_at: ..time) }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def reactivatable?(now: Time.current)
    cancelled? && cancelled_at > now - CANCELLATION_WINDOW
  end

  def reactivate_by
    cancelled_at + CANCELLATION_WINDOW if cancelled?
  end

  # Marks the account cancelled and signs out every user in it.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      raise StateError.new("already_cancelled", "This account is already cancelled.") if cancelled?

      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!(now: Time.current)
    with_lock do
      raise StateError.new("not_cancelled", "This account is not cancelled.") unless cancelled?
      raise StateError.new("reactivation_window_closed", "This account was cancelled more than 90 days ago and can no longer be reactivated.") unless reactivatable?(now: now)

      update!(cancelled_at: nil)
    end
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts cancelled more than CANCELLATION_WINDOW ago, with
  # all their data. Returns the number of accounts deleted.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - CANCELLATION_WINDOW

    cancelled_before(cutoff).pluck(:id).count do |id|
      transaction do
        # Re-check under a row lock: the owner may have reactivated since the scan.
        account = lock.cancelled_before(cutoff).find_by(id: id)
        next false unless account

        account.destroy!
        true
      end
    end
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      status: cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active",
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      reactivate_by: reactivate_by,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def subdomain_not_reserved
    errors.add(:subdomain, "is reserved") if RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS.include?(subdomain)
  end
end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# One-time links sent by email. Only one token per user and purpose exists at a
# time, so requesting a new link invalidates the previous one.
class UserToken < ApplicationRecord
  LIFETIMES = {
    "email_verification" => 3.days,
    "password_reset" => 1.hour
  }.freeze

  belongs_to :user

  validates :purpose, inclusion: { in: LIFETIMES.keys }

  # Replaces any earlier token for this user and purpose. Returns the raw token
  # for the email link; the database keeps only its digest.
  def self.issue!(user, purpose)
    purpose = purpose.to_s
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)

    transaction do
      user.user_tokens.where(purpose: purpose).delete_all
      user.user_tokens.create!(
        purpose: purpose,
        token_digest: digest(raw),
        expires_at: LIFETIMES.fetch(purpose).from_now
      )
    end

    raw
  end

  # Returns the unexpired token record matching a raw token, or nil.
  def self.redeem(purpose, raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    record = find_by(purpose: purpose.to_s, token_digest: digest(raw))
    record if record && record.expires_at > Time.current
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end
end
# An invitation for someone to join the business as an admin or an agent. The emailed
# link carries a token; the database keeps only its digest.
#
# Status comes from the timestamps:
#   accepted - the invitee signed up through the link
#   revoked  - an admin revoked it
#   expired  - it passed expires_at without being accepted or revoked
#   pending  - none of the above, so the link works
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  LIFETIME = 7.days
  ROLES = [User::ADMIN, User::AGENT].freeze

  PENDING = "pending".freeze
  ACCEPTED = "accepted".freeze
  REVOKED = "revoked".freeze
  EXPIRED = "expired".freeze
  STATUSES = [PENDING, ACCEPTED, REVOKED, EXPIRED].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.strip.downcase }

  validates :email,
            presence: true,
            length: { maximum: 255 },
            format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, inclusion: { in: ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent" }
  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  # Creating or resending an invitation must not compete with a pending one or a member.
  validate :email_available, on: %i[issue resend]

  # Neither accepted nor revoked. Expiry is checked separately because it depends on the time.
  scope :unresolved, -> { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) { unresolved.where(arel_table[:expires_at].gt(now)) }
  scope :expired, ->(now = Time.current) { unresolved.where(arel_table[:expires_at].lteq(now)) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }

  # Filters by a status name from the API. Each scope matches exactly the invitations whose
  # #status is that value.
  def self.with_status(status, now: Time.current)
    case status
    when PENDING then pending(now)
    when ACCEPTED then accepted
    when REVOKED then revoked
    when EXPIRED then expired(now)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status: #{status}"
    end
  end

  # Returns the invitation for a raw token, whatever its status.
  def self.find_by_token(raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
  end

  # Invites someone to the business. Returns [invitation, raw_token]; the caller emails the
  # token. Refused while the email belongs to a member or already has a pending invitation.
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:, now: Time.current)
    raw = new_token
    invitation = nil

    transaction do
      # Locking the business serializes invitations and registrations, so two requests
      # cannot both pass the checks for the same email.
      account.lock!
      invitation = account.invitations.new(
        invited_by: invited_by,
        email: email,
        role: role,
        token_digest: digest(raw),
        expires_at: now + LIFETIME
      )
      invitation.save!(context: :issue)
    end

    [invitation, raw]
  end

  # True when a pending invitation exists for this email, so customers cannot register with it.
  def self.pending_for_email?(account, email, now: Time.current)
    account.invitations.pending(now).exists?(email: email)
  end

  def self.new_token
    SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)
  end

  # Issues a new link that is valid for the full LIFETIME, and stops the old link working.
  # Only pending and expired invitations can be resent. Returns the raw token.
  def resend!(now: Time.current)
    raw = self.class.new_token

    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!
      self.token_digest = self.class.digest(raw)
      self.expires_at = now + LIFETIME
      save!(context: :resend)
    end

    raw
  end

  # Revokes the invitation so its link stops working. Accepted and already revoked
  # invitations cannot be revoked.
  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_open!
      update!(revoked_at: now)
    end
  end

  # Creates the invitee's account with the invited role and a verified email, and marks the
  # invitation accepted. Returns the new user. If the user is invalid, nothing is saved.
  def accept!(name:, password:, now: Time.current)
    user = nil

    account.with_lock do
      lock!
      ensure_pending!(now: now)
      # The invitation link proves the invitee owns the email, so no verification email is needed.
      user = account.users.create!(name: name, email: email, password: password, role: role, verified_at: now)
      update!(accepted_at: now)
    end

    user
  end

  def status(now: Time.current)
    if accepted?
      ACCEPTED
    elsif revoked?
      REVOKED
    elsif expires_at <= now
      EXPIRED
    else
      PENDING
    end
  end

  def pending?(now: Time.current)
    status(now: now) == PENDING
  end

  # Raises unless the link can still be used to accept the invitation.
  def ensure_pending!(now: Time.current)
    ensure_open!
    return if pending?(now: now)

    raise StateError.new("invitation_expired", "This invitation has expired. Ask an admin to send it again.")
  end

  def accepted?
    accepted_at.present?
  end

  def revoked?
    revoked_at.present?
  end

  # The admin's view of an invitation. Never includes the token.
  def as_api_json(now: Time.current)
    {
      id: id,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      status: status(now: now),
      expires_at: expires_at,
      accepted_at: accepted_at,
      revoked_at: revoked_at,
      invited_by: invited_by && { id: invited_by.id, name: invited_by.name },
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  # What the acceptance screen shows before the invitee signs up.
  def as_preview_api_json
    {
      email: email,
      role: role,
      business_name: account.name,
      subdomain: account.subdomain,
      expires_at: expires_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_open!
    raise StateError.new("invitation_accepted", "This invitation has already been accepted.") if accepted?
    raise StateError.new("invitation_revoked", "This invitation was revoked. Send a new invitation instead.") if revoked?
  end

  def email_available
    return if email.blank? || account.nil?

    if account.users.exists?(email: email)
      errors.add(:email, "already belongs to someone in this business")
    elsif account.invitations.pending.where(email: email).where.not(id: id).exists?
"

  rescue_from StateError, with: :render_state_error
  rescue_from RequestFilter::Invalid, with: :render_invalid_filter

  private

  # Strict true/false for flags such as suspended=true. Unlike ActiveModel's casting, any
  # other value is nil, not true.
  def parse_boolean(value)
    case value
    when true, "true" then true
    when false, "false" then false
    end
  end

  # The "envelope" object for a request, e.g. params[:session] in {"session": {...}}.
  # A missing or non-object value is a 400, not a server error. Pass `parent` for an
  # object nested in another envelope, e.g. the comment in {"ticket": {"comment": {...}}}.
  def require_envelope(key, parent = params)
    value = parent.require(key)
    raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, key unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    value
  end

  # Every error uses the same shape: { error: { code, message, details? } }.
  def render_error(status, code, message, details: nil)
    body = { code: code, message: message }
    body[:details] = details if details.present?
    render json: { error: body }, status: status
  end

  def render_record_invalid(exception)
    record = exception.record
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence, details: record.errors.to_hash)
  end

  def render_parameter_missing(exception)
    render_error(400, "parameter_missing", exception.message)
  end

  def render_invalid_json(_exception)
    render_error(400, "invalid_json", "The request body must be valid JSON.")
  end

  def render_state_error(exception)
    render_error(422, exception.code, exception.message)
  end

  def render_invalid_filter(exception)
    render_error(400, "invalid_filter", exception.message)
  end
end
# Resolves the business a request is about from the X-Helpdesk-Account header.
module AccountContext
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def requested_subdomain
    request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase.presence
  end

  # For public endpoints that need to know the business (sign-in, portal, ...).
  def load_account_from_header!
    subdomain = requested_subdomain
    return render_error(400, "account_required", "Send the X-Helpdesk-Account header with the business subdomain.") if subdomain.nil?

    @account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
    render_error(404, "account_not_found", "No business has that subdomain.") unless @account
  end

  # True when no account header was sent, or the header names this account.
  def requested_account_matches?(account)
    requested_subdomain.nil? || requested_subdomain == account.subdomain
  end

  # Ordinary business access stops once the account is cancelled.
  def require_active_account!
    return unless @account.cancelled?

    render_error(403, "account_cancelled", "This account has been cancelled.")
  end
end

    # Customers sign themselves up for a business's portal. They verify their email, then
    # use the same sign-in, profile and password flows as everyone else.
    class RegistrationsController < ApplicationController
      before_action :load_account_from_header!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      # POST /api/v1/registrations
      # { user: { name, email, password } } with X-Helpdesk-Account
      def create
        # Only these fields are accepted. Everyone who registers here is a customer.
        user = @account.users.new(require_envelope(:user).permit(:name, :email, :password).merge(role: User::CUSTOMER))

          @account.lock!
          # An email with a pending invitation is reserved for that invitee. The message is
          # worded so it does not reveal the invitation.
          if Invitation.pending_for_email?(@account, user.email)
            user.errors.add(:email, "can't be used to register with this business")
            raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, user
          end

          user.save!
          token = UserToken.issue!(user, :email_verification)
        end
        # Send only after commit, so the link never points at a rolled-back user.
        UserMailer.email_verification(user, token).deliver_later

        render json: { user: user.as_api_json }, status: :created
      rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
        # Lost a race with another registration for the same email.
        render_error(422, "validation_failed", "That email is already registered with this business.")
      end
    end

      before_action :authenticate_session!, only: :destroy

      # POST /api/v1/sessions

          return render_error(403, "account_cancelled", "This account has been cancelled.")

          session: { token: session.token, id: session.id, created_at: session.created_at },
          user: user.as_api_json,
          account: @account.as_api_json

  module Settings
    DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze

# Lets the separate frontend app (HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL) call this API from browsers.
#
# Only the configured frontend origin gets CORS headers; other origins are
# untouched, so browsers block them. Auth uses bearer tokens rather than cookies,
# so credentialed requests are not enabled.
#
# This lives in an initializer, not lib/, because initializers run before
# Zeitwerk autoloading is ready.
module Helpdesk
  class Cors
    ALLOWED_METHODS = "GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS".freeze
    ALLOWED_HEADERS = "Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, X-Helpdesk-Account".freeze
    MAX_AGE = "600".freeze

    def initialize(app)
      @app = app
    end

    def call(env)
      origin = env["HTTP_ORIGIN"]
      return @app.call(env) unless origin && allowed_origin?(origin)

      return [204, preflight_headers(origin), []] if preflight?(env)

      status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
      headers = headers.merge("access-control-allow-origin" => origin)
      headers["vary"] = [headers["vary"], "Origin"].compact.join(", ")
      [status, headers, body]
    end

    private

    def allowed_origin?(origin)
      origin.casecmp?(Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_origin)
    end

    def preflight?(env)
      env["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "OPTIONS" && env["HTTP_ACCESS_CONTROL_REQUEST_METHOD"].present?
    end

      def update
        attrs = require_envelope(:ticket)

        reply = {}
        if attrs.key?(:comment)
          comment = require_envelope(:comment, attrs).permit(:body, :public)
          reply[:body] = comment[:body].to_s
          # Replies are public unless staff mark them as private notes.
          reply[:public] = comment[:public] if comment.key?(:public)
        end
        reply[:status] = attrs.permit(:status)[:status].to_s if attrs.key?(:status)
        # A null priority becomes "", which fails validation, so a priority cannot be cleared.
        reply[:priority] = attrs.permit(:priority)[:priority].to_s if attrs.key?(:priority)
        if attrs.key?(:assignee_id)
          assignee_id = parse_assignee_id(attrs[:assignee_id])
          return render_invalid_assignee if assignee_id == INVALID_ASSIGNEE

          reply[:assignee_id] = assignee_id
        end

        @ticket.staff_reply!(author: @current_user, **reply)
        render json: { ticket: @ticket.as_ticket_api_json }
      end

      # GET /api/v1/tickets/:id/comments

        records, paging = paginate(@ticket.comments.includes(:author))
        render json: { comments: records.map(&:as_api_json), **paging }

# A signed-in session. The client holds the raw bearer token; only its SHA-256
# digest is stored, so a database leak does not expose usable tokens.
class Session < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user

  # The raw token. Set only on the object returned by start_for; never persisted.
  attr_accessor :token

  def self.start_for(user)
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw))
    session.token = raw
    session
  end

  # Returns the session for a raw bearer token, with its user and account loaded.
  # A suspended user's session is not valid, even if one somehow survived the suspension.
  def self.lookup(raw)
    return if raw.blank?

    session = includes(user: :account).find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
    session unless session&.user&.suspended?
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw)

module ActionMailbox
  # The base class for all Action Mailbox ingress controllers.
  class BaseController < ActionController::Base
    skip_forgery_protection

    before_action :ensure_configured

    private
      def ensure_configured
        unless ActionMailbox.ingress == ingress_name
          head :not_found
        end
      end

      def ingress_name
        self.class.name.remove(/\AActionMailbox::Ingresses::/, /::InboundEmailsController\z/).underscore.to_sym
      end


      def authenticate_by_password
        if password.present?
          http_basic_authenticate_or_request_with name: "actionmailbox", password: password, realm: "Action Mailbox"
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Missing required ingress credentials"
        end
      end

      def password
        Rails.application.credentials.dig(:action_mailbox, :ingress_password) || ENV["RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD"]
      end
  end

require "mail"

module ActionMailbox
  # The +InboundEmail+ is an Active Record that keeps a reference to the raw email stored in Active Storage
  # and tracks the status of processing. By default, incoming emails will go through the following lifecycle:
  #
  # * Pending: Just received by one of the ingress controllers and scheduled for routing.
  # * Processing: During active processing, while a specific mailbox is running its #process method.
  # * Delivered: Successfully processed by the specific mailbox.
  # * Failed: An exception was raised during the specific mailbox's execution of the +#process+ method.
  # * Bounced: Rejected processing by the specific mailbox and bounced to sender.
  #
  # Once the +InboundEmail+ has reached the status of being either +delivered+, +failed+, or +bounced+,
  # it'll count as having been +#processed?+. Once processed, the +InboundEmail+ will be scheduled for
  # automatic incineration at a later point.
  #
  # When working with an +InboundEmail+, you'll usually interact with the parsed version of the source,
  # which is available as a +Mail+ object from +#mail+. But you can also access the raw source directly
  # using the +#source+ method.
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  #   inbound_email.mail.from # => 'david@loudthinking.com'
  #   inbound_email.source # Returns the full rfc822 source of the email as text
  class InboundEmail < Record
    include Incineratable, MessageId, Routable

    has_one_attached :raw_email, service: ActionMailbox.storage_service
    enum :status, %i[ pending processing delivered failed bounced ]

    def mail
      @mail ||= Mail.from_source(source)
    end

    def source
      @source ||= raw_email.download
    end

    def processed?
      delivered? || failed? || bounced?
    end

    def instrumentation_payload # :nodoc:
      {
        id: id,
        message_id: message_id,
        status: status
      }
    end
  end
end

ActiveSupport.run_load_hooks :action_mailbox_inbound_email, ActionMailbox::InboundEmail

  # You can disable incinerating processed emails by setting +config.action_mailbox.incinerate+ or
  # +ActionMailbox.incinerate+ to +false+.
  class IncinerationJob < ActiveJob::Base
    queue_as { ActionMailbox.queues[:incineration] }

    discard_on ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound

    def self.schedule(inbound_email)
      set(wait: ActionMailbox.incinerate_after).perform_later(inbound_email)
    end

    def perform(inbound_email)
      inbound_email.incinerate
    end
  end
end

# A newly received +InboundEmail+ will not be routed synchronously as part of ingress controller's receival.
# Instead, the routing will be done asynchronously, using a +RoutingJob+, to ensure maximum parallel capacity.

# By default, all newly created +InboundEmail+ records that have the status of +pending+, which is the default,

module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::Routable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :route_later, if: :pending?
  end

  # Enqueue a +RoutingJob+ for this +InboundEmail+.

    ActionMailbox::RoutingJob.perform_later self
  end

  # Route this +InboundEmail+ using the routing rules declared on the +ApplicationMailbox+.
  def route
    ApplicationMailbox.route self
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# The +Message-ID+ as specified by rfc822 is supposed to be a unique identifier for that individual email.
# That makes it an ideal tracking token for debugging and forensics, just like +X-Request-Id+ does for
# web request.
#
# If an inbound email does not, against the rfc822 mandate, specify a Message-ID, one will be generated
# using the approach from +Mail::MessageIdField+.
module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::MessageId
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    # Create a new +InboundEmail+ from the raw +source+ of the email, which is uploaded as an Active Storage
    # attachment called +raw_email+. Before the upload, extract the Message-ID from the +source+ and set
    # it as an attribute on the new +InboundEmail+.
    def create_and_extract_message_id!(source, **options)
      message_checksum = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(source)
      message_id = extract_message_id(source) || generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)

      create! raw_email: create_and_upload_raw_email!(source),
        message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum, **options
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      nil
    end

    private
      def extract_message_id(source)
        Mail.from_source(source).message_id rescue nil
      end

      def generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)
        Mail::MessageIdField.new("<#{message_checksum}@#{::Socket.gethostname}.mail>").message_id.tap do |message_id|
          logger.warn "Message-ID couldn't be parsed or is missing. Generated a new Message-ID: #{message_id}"
        end
      end

      def create_and_upload_raw_email!(source)
        ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload! io: StringIO.new(source), filename: "message.eml", content_type: "message/rfc822",
                                               service_name: ActionMailbox.storage_service
      end
  end
end

require "active_support/rescuable"

require "action_mailbox/callbacks"
require "action_mailbox/routing"

module ActionMailbox
  # = Action Mailbox \Base
  #
  # The base class for all application mailboxes. Not intended to be inherited from directly. Inherit from
  # +ApplicationMailbox+ instead, as that's where the app-specific routing is configured. This routing
  # is specified in the following ways:
  #
  #   class ApplicationMailbox < ActionMailbox::Base
  #     # Any of the recipients of the mail (whether to, cc, bcc) are matched against the regexp.
  #     routing /^replies@/i => :replies
  #
  #     # Any of the recipients of the mail (whether to, cc, bcc) needs to be an exact match for the string.
  #     routing "help@example.com" => :help
  #
  #     # Any callable (proc, lambda, etc) object is passed the inbound_email record and is a match if true.
  #     routing ->(inbound_email) { inbound_email.mail.to.size > 2 } => :multiple_recipients
  #
  #     # Any object responding to #match? is called with the inbound_email record as an argument. Match if true.
  #     routing CustomAddress.new => :custom
  #
  #     # Any inbound_email that has not been already matched will be sent to the BackstopMailbox.
  #     routing :all => :backstop
  #   end
  #
  # Application mailboxes need to override the #process method, which is invoked by the framework after
  # callbacks have been run. The callbacks available are: +before_processing+, +after_processing+, and
  # +around_processing+. The primary use case is to ensure that certain preconditions to processing are fulfilled
  # using +before_processing+ callbacks.
  #
  # If a precondition fails to be met, you can halt the processing using the +#bounced!+ method,
  # which will silently prevent any further processing, but not actually send out any bounce notice. You
  # can also pair this behavior with the invocation of an Action Mailer class responsible for sending out
  # an actual bounce email. This is done using the #bounce_with method, which takes the mail object returned
  # by an Action Mailer method, like so:
  #
  #   class ForwardsMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  #     before_processing :ensure_sender_is_a_user
  #
  #     private
  #       def ensure_sender_is_a_user
  #         unless User.exists?(email_address: mail.from)
  #           bounce_with UserRequiredMailer.missing(inbound_email)
  #         end
  #       end
  #   end
  #
  # During the processing of the inbound email, the status will be tracked. Before processing begins,
  # the email will normally have the +pending+ status. Once processing begins, just before callbacks
  # and the #process method is called, the status is changed to +processing+. If processing is allowed to
  # complete, the status is changed to +delivered+. If a bounce is triggered, then +bounced+. If an unhandled
  # exception is bubbled up, then +failed+.
  #
  # Exceptions can be handled at the class level using the familiar
  # ActiveSupport::Rescuable approach:
  #
  #   class ForwardsMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  #     rescue_from(ApplicationSpecificVerificationError) { bounced! }
  #   end
  class Base
    include ActiveSupport::Rescuable
    include ActionMailbox::Callbacks, ActionMailbox::Routing

    attr_reader :inbound_email
    delegate :mail, :delivered!, :bounced!, to: :inbound_email

    delegate :logger, to: ActionMailbox

    def self.receive(inbound_email)
      new(inbound_email).perform_processing
    end

    def initialize(inbound_email)
      @inbound_email = inbound_email
    end

    def perform_processing # :nodoc:
      ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument "process.action_mailbox", instrumentation_payload do
        track_status_of_inbound_email do
          run_callbacks :process do
            process
          end
        end
      rescue => exception
        # TODO: Include a reference to the inbound_email in the exception raised so error handling becomes easier
        rescue_with_handler(exception) || raise
      end
    end

    def process
      # Override in subclasses
    end

    def finished_processing? # :nodoc:
      inbound_email.delivered? || inbound_email.bounced?
    end

    # Enqueues the given +message+ for delivery and changes the inbound email's status to +:bounced+.
    def bounce_with(message)
      inbound_email.bounced!
      message.deliver_later
    end

    # Immediately sends the given +message+ and changes the inbound email's status to +:bounced+.
    def bounce_now_with(message)
      inbound_email.bounced!
      message.deliver_now
    end

    private
      def instrumentation_payload
        {
          mailbox: self,
          inbound_email: inbound_email.instrumentation_payload
        }
      end

      def track_status_of_inbound_email
        inbound_email.processing!
        yield
        inbound_email.delivered! unless inbound_email.bounced?
      rescue
        inbound_email.failed!
        raise
      end
  end
end

module ActionMailbox
  # = Action Mailbox \Router
  #
  # Encapsulates the routes that live on the ApplicationMailbox and performs the actual routing when
  # an inbound_email is received.
  class Router
    class RoutingError < StandardError; end

    def initialize
      @routes = []
    end

    def add_routes(routes)
      routes.each do |(address, mailbox_name)|
        add_route address, to: mailbox_name
      end
    end

    def add_route(address, to:)
      routes.append Route.new(address, to: to)
    end

    def route(inbound_email)
      if mailbox = mailbox_for(inbound_email)
        mailbox.receive(inbound_email)
      else
        inbound_email.bounced!

        raise RoutingError
      end
    end

    def mailbox_for(inbound_email)
      routes.detect { |route| route.match?(inbound_email) }&.mailbox_class
    end

    private
      attr_reader :routes
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActionMailbox
  # Encapsulates a route, which can then be matched against an inbound_email and provide a lookup of the matching
  # mailbox class. See examples for the different route addresses and how to use them in the ActionMailbox::Base
  # documentation.
  class Router::Route
    attr_reader :address, :mailbox_name

    def initialize(address, to:)
      @address, @mailbox_name = address, to

      ensure_valid_address
    end

    def match?(inbound_email)
      case address
      when :all
        true
      when String
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.casecmp?(recipient) }
      when Regexp
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.match?(recipient) }
      when Proc
        address.call(inbound_email)
      else
        address.match?(inbound_email)
      end
    end

    def mailbox_class
      "#{mailbox_name.to_s.camelize}Mailbox".constantize
    end

    private
      def ensure_valid_address
        unless [ Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc ].any? { |klass| address.is_a?(klass) } || address.respond_to?(:match?)
          raise ArgumentError, "Expected a Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc, or matchable, got #{address.inspect}"
        end
      end
  end
end

module ActionMailbox
  # = Action Mailbox \Callbacks
  #
  # Defines the callbacks related to processing.
  module Callbacks
    extend  ActiveSupport::Concern
    include ActiveSupport::Callbacks

    TERMINATOR = ->(mailbox, chain) do
      chain.call
      mailbox.finished_processing?
    end

    included do
      define_callbacks :process, terminator: TERMINATOR, skip_after_callbacks_if_terminated: true

    class_methods do
      def before_processing(*methods, &block)

      end

      def after_processing(*methods, &block)
        set_callback(:process, :after, *methods, &block)
      end

      def around_processing(*methods, &block)
        set_callback(:process, :around, *methods, &block)

module ActionMailbox
  # Command class for carrying out the actual incineration of the +InboundMail+ that's been scheduled
  # for removal. Before the incineration – which really is just a call to +#destroy!+ – is run, we verify
  # that it's both eligible (by virtue of having already been processed) and time to do so (that is,
  # the +InboundEmail+ was processed after the +incinerate_after+ time).
  class InboundEmail::Incineratable::Incineration
    def initialize(inbound_email)
      @inbound_email = inbound_email
    end

    def run
      @inbound_email.destroy! if due? && processed?
    end

    private
      def due?
        @inbound_email.updated_at < ActionMailbox.incinerate_after.ago.end_of_day
      end

      def processed?
        @inbound_email.processed?
      end
  end
end

=== pagination ===
# Offset pagination for list endpoints: ?page=1&per_page=25.
#
# A page or per_page that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 400. A per_page above
# MAX_PER_PAGE is capped, and the response shows the value actually used.
module Pagination
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  class InvalidPage < StandardError; end

  included do
    rescue_from InvalidPage do |error|
      render_error(400, "invalid_pagination", error.message)
    end
  end

  private

  # Returns [records, paging] for one page of the scope. `paging` is the set of fields
  # that go next to the records in the response.
  def paginate(scope)
    page = page_number(:page, default: 1)
    per_page = [page_number(:per_page, default: DEFAULT_PER_PAGE), MAX_PER_PAGE].min

    count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
    # Skip the query for pages past the end. This also keeps huge page numbers out of SQL.
    records = offset < count ? scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a : []

    paging = {
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
    [records, paging]
  end

  def page_number(name, default:)
    raw = params[name]
    return default if raw.blank?

    value = Integer(raw.to_s, 10, exception: false)
    raise InvalidPage, "#{name} must be a whole number, 1 or more." if value.nil? || value < 1

    value
  end
end

I have enough information to write the implementation. The design:

- **Addresses.** Business mail goes to `<subdomain>@<support domain>`. Each email-origin request gets a private `reply+<32-hex>@<support domain>` address. The `+` can't appear in a subdomain, so the two forms can't collide.
- **Mailbox.** Everything routes to `SupportMailbox`. Each delivery runs in one savepoint-wrapped transaction under the business row lock. The Message-ID is claimed last, through the partial unique index. Any rejection rolls back everything the delivery wrote, so a retry is never blocked.
- **Outbound.** A staff public reply on an email request is emailed to the requester, with `Reply-To` set to the private address and threading headers.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/support_address.rb <<'EOF'
# The addresses that support mail is sent to, and what a given address is for.
#
# Each business has a plain address, <subdomain>@<support domain>, such as acme@support.example.test.
# Mail to it opens a new request.
#
# Each request opened by email also has a private reply address, reply+<token>@<support domain>.
# Mail to it is a reply on that request. The "+" keeps it apart from business addresses, since a
# subdomain cannot contain "+".
module SupportAddress
  REPLY_LOCAL_PART = /\Areply\+(?<token>[0-9a-f]{32})\z/

  module_function

  def domain
    Helpdesk::Settings.support_domain
  end

  def for_account(account)
    "#{account.subdomain}@#{domain}"
  end

  def reply_for(request)
    "reply+#{request.reply_token}@#{domain}"
  end

  # Returns [:business, subdomain] or [:reply, token] for an address on the support domain, or nil
  # for anything else.
  def parse(address)
    address = Mail::Address.new(address.to_s).address
    local, host = address.to_s.downcase.split("@", 2)
    return unless host == domain

    if (match = REPLY_LOCAL_PART.match(local))
      [:reply, match[:token]]
    elsif local.match?(Account::SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT)
      [:business, local]
    end
  rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
    nil
  end
end
EOF
cat > app/models/automated_mail.rb <<'EOF'
# Mail that a machine sent: auto-replies, bounces, delivery reports and mailing-list posts.
# Support does not act on it, so two machines cannot answer each other.
class AutomatedMail
  # Other than "no", Auto-Submitted marks a machine-generated message (RFC 3834).
  AUTO_RESPONSE_HEADERS = %w[X-Autoreply X-Autorespond X-Auto-Response-Suppress].freeze
  BULK_PRECEDENCE = %w[bulk list junk auto_reply].freeze
  REPORT_TYPES = %w[multipart/report message/delivery-status message/disposition-notification].freeze
  MACHINE_SENDERS = %w[mailer-daemon postmaster noreply no-reply donotreply do-not-reply].freeze

  def initialize(mail)
    @mail = mail
  end

  def automated?
    auto_submitted? || bulk? || list_mail? || auto_response? || null_sender? || report? || machine_sender?
  end

  private

  def auto_submitted?
    value = header_value("Auto-Submitted")
    !value.nil? && value.strip.downcase != "no"
  end

  def bulk?
    BULK_PRECEDENCE.include?(header_value("Precedence").to_s.strip.downcase)
  end

  def list_mail?
    @mail.header.fields.any? { |field| field.name.downcase.start_with?("list-") }
  end

  def auto_response?
    AUTO_RESPONSE_HEADERS.any? { |name| @mail.header[name] }
  end

  # Bounces are sent from an empty return path, "<>", which Mail reads back as an empty value.
  def null_sender?
    field = @mail.header["Return-Path"]
    !field.nil? && field.value.to_s.strip.empty?
  end

  def report?
    REPORT_TYPES.include?(@mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase)
  end

  def machine_sender?
    local_part = @mail.from.first.to_s.split("@").first.to_s.downcase
    MACHINE_SENDERS.include?(local_part)
  end

  def header_value(name)
    @mail.header[name]&.value
  end
end
EOF
cat > app/models/mail_text.rb <<'EOF'
# The plain-text body of an email. This is the text/plain part when there is one, and otherwise
# the text/html part converted to text. Attachments are ignored.
class MailText
  NUL = "\u0000".freeze

  # Returns the body as UTF-8 text with Unix line endings, or nil when the message has no text.
  def self.from(mail)
    new(mail).body
  end

  def initialize(mail)
    @mail = mail
  end

  def body
    text = plain_text || html_text
    text && normalize(text).presence
  end

  private

  def plain_text
    first_part("text/plain")&.decoded
  end

  def html_text
    html = first_part("text/html")&.decoded
    html && html_to_text(html)
  end

  def first_part(type)
    candidates = @mail.multipart? ? @mail.all_parts : [@mail]
    candidates.find { |part| part.mime_type == type && !part.attachment? }
  end

  # Drops what a reader does not see, then turns the remaining markup into line breaks and text.
  def html_to_text(html)
    document = Nokogiri::HTML5(html)
    document.css("head, script, style").each(&:remove)
    document.css("br").each { |line_break| line_break.replace("\n") }
    document.css("p, div, li, tr, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6").each { |block| block.after("\n") }
    document.text
  end

  # Valid UTF-8 with Unix line endings. PostgreSQL cannot store NUL characters, so they go too.
  def normalize(text)
    text.to_s.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace).scrub("")
        .delete(NUL).gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
  end
end
EOF

# Staff replies on requests opened by email. The reply goes to the requester. Reply-To is the
# request's private reply address, so their next email comes back to this request.
class TicketMailer < ApplicationMailer

    @comment = comment

      subject: "Re: #{@request.subject}",
      reply_to: SupportAddress.reply_for(@request),
      in_reply_to: origin,

    )
  end
end

steps.message: Now the core piece, the mailbox. Every delivery is processed in one savepoint-wrapped transaction under the business row lock. The Message-ID is claimed last. Any rejection rolls back everything it wrote, so a retry starts clean.

arguments.command:
cd /app && mkdir -p app/mailboxes && cat > app/mailboxes/application_mailbox.rb <<'EOF'
# Every inbound message goes to SupportMailbox, which decides what it means.
class ApplicationMailbox < ActionMailbox::Base
  routing :all => :support
end
EOF
cat > app/mailboxes/support_mailbox.rb <<'EOF'
# Handles mail sent to a business's support address, or to a request's private reply address.
#
# Mail to the plain address opens a new request for the sender. If the sender is not yet a user
# of the business, they become a customer: unverified, and sent a verification link. Receiving
# mail never verifies anyone.
#
# Mail to a request's reply address is a reply on that request. Only its requester may send one.
#
# Mail that cannot be used is ignored: nothing is saved, nothing is sent back, and the Message-ID is
# left unclaimed, so a corrected retry with the same Message-ID is processed normally.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  # Stops processing with a reason. Nothing is sent to the sender.
  class Rejected < StandardError; end

  NO_SUBJECT = "(no subject)".freeze

  def process
    reject!("automated or list mail") if AutomatedMail.new(mail).automated?
    reject!("no sender address") if sender.empty?
    reject!("sent from the support domain") if sender.end_with?("@#{SupportAddress.domain}")
    reject!("no message text") if text.nil?
    reject!("already processed") if already_delivered?

    verification = deliver
    UserMailer.email_verification(*verification).deliver_later if verification
  rescue Rejected => error
    ignore!(error.message)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    ignore!(error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
  end

  private

  # Saves the request or reply, and claims the Message-ID, in one transaction. Returns [user, token]
  # when a new customer was created, so their verification link is sent only after the commit.
  #
  # The savepoint makes a rejection roll back everything the delivery wrote, even when this runs
  # inside an outer transaction.
  def deliver
    account, reply_token = target
    verification = nil

    Account.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      # Locking the business serializes deliveries with each other, with invitations and with
      # registrations, and makes the cancelled check current.
      account.lock!
      reject!("the business is cancelled") if account.cancelled?

      request = reply_token && account.requests.find_by(reply_token: reply_token)
      if request
        reply_to(request)
      else
        verification = open_request(account)
      end

      claim_message_id!
    end

    verification
  end

  # The business this message is for, and the reply token when it is a reply. Mail for no
  # business, or for more than one, is ignored. An unknown reply token is ignored too, so the
  # plain address still opens a new request.
  def target
    addresses = mail.recipients.filter_map { |address| SupportAddress.parse(address) }
    tokens = addresses.filter_map { |kind, value| value if kind == :reply }.uniq
    subdomains = addresses.filter_map { |kind, value| value if kind == :business }.uniq
    reject!("replies to more than one request") if tokens.many?

    reply_request = tokens.first && Request.find_by(reply_token: tokens.first)
    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: subdomains).to_a
    accounts |= [reply_request.account] if reply_request
    reject!("not addressed to a business") if accounts.empty?
    reject!("addressed to more than one business") if accounts.many?

    [accounts.first, reply_request&.reply_token]
  end

  # Only the requester may reply. Replies to pending or solved requests reopen them.
  def reply_to(request)
    requester = request.requester
    reject!("only the requester can reply by email") unless requester.email == sender
    reject!("the requester is suspended") if requester.suspended?

    request.requester_reply!(author: requester, body: body)
  end

  def open_request(account)
    requester, token = requester_for_sender(account)
    Request.open_from_email!(requester: requester, subject: subject, body: body, message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
    token && [requester, token]
  end

  # The existing user with the sender's address, or a new customer. A new customer is unverified
  # and gets a random password nobody knows. They verify through the emailed link, then choose a
  # password with a password reset.
  def requester_for_sender(account)
    existing = account.users.find_by(email: sender)
    if existing
      reject!("the sender is suspended") if existing.suspended?
      return [existing, nil]
    end

    # A pending invitation reserves the address, as it does for registration.
    reject!("the address has a pending invitation") if Invitation.pending_for_email?(account, sender)

    customer = account.users.create!(
      name: sender_name,
      email: sender,
      role: User::CUSTOMER,
      password: SecureRandom.hex(32)
    )
    [customer, UserToken.issue!(customer, :email_verification)]
  end

  # Marks the delivery processed. Two deliveries with one Message-ID can race here: the database
  # lets only one through, and the other rolls back everything it wrote.
  def claim_message_id!
    inbound_email.delivered!
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    reject!("already processed")
  end

  def already_delivered?
    ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.delivered
                               .where(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
                               .where.not(id: inbound_email.id)
                               .exists?
  end

  def ignore!(reason)
    logger.info("Inbound mail #{inbound_email.id} (#{inbound_email.message_id}) was not processed: #{reason}.")
    # Ends processing without sending a bounce message.
    bounced!
  end

  def reject!(reason)
    raise Rejected, reason
  end

  def sender
    @sender ||= Array(mail.from).first.to_s.strip.downcase
  end

  def sender_name
    name = clean_line(mail.from_address&.display_name)
    (name.presence || sender.split("@").first).truncate(User::NAME_MAX_LENGTH)
  end

  def subject
    clean_line(mail.subject).presence&.truncate(Request::SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH) || NO_SUBJECT
  end

  def body
    text.truncate(Comment::BODY_MAX_LENGTH)
  end

  def text
    @text ||= MailText.from(mail)
  end

  # A single line of text with no NUL characters or invalid UTF-8.
  def clean_line(value)
    value.to_s.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace).scrub("").delete("\u0000").squish
  end
end
EOF

steps.message:
Two things to note from this run:

- Without auth the relay returns `401`, so the password gate works.
- The mailbox raises `NotImplementedError` in `deliver`, and the cause is the gem, not my code. After the message is claimed, the gem schedules incineration 30 days out with `set(wait:)`. The inline adapter in test refuses delayed jobs.

Disabling incineration in the test environment is the clean fix, because tests don't need raw-email cleanup. Production keeps the async adapter, which supports delays.

steps.message: The mailbox is fine; my test helper is wrong. Mail's `attachments[]=` on an already-set plain body replaces it, so the attachment fixture had no text part at all. The mailbox correctly refused it as "no message text". I'll fix the helper so it builds a proper multipart message with the text part kept.

arguments.command:

      message.content_type = "text/html; charset=UTF-8"
      message.body = html

    else
      message.body = body
    end
    message.attachments["notes.txt"] = { mime_type: "text/plain", content: attachment } if attachment
    message.to_s

new = """    if html && body.nil?
      message.content_type = "text/html; charset=UTF-8"
      message.body = html
    elsif html || attachment
      # Parts are set explicitly: adding an attachment to a single-part message would drop its body.

      message.attachments["notes.txt"] = { mime_type: "text/plain", content: attachment } if attachment
    else

    end
