steps.message: Next, the reply tests. They cover both directions: outbound staff replies, and the requester's replies arriving at the private address. They also include the round trip, where the `Reply-To` from a real staff email is used to reply.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > test/integration/email_replies_test.rb <<'EOF'
require "test_helper"

# Replies in both directions on requests opened by email: staff replies go out to the requester,
# and the requester's replies come back to the same request through its private reply address.
class EmailRepliesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @owner_token = owner_session.dig("session", "token")
    add_staff!(email: "sam@acme.test", role: "agent")
    @agent_token = sign_in!(email: "sam@acme.test").dig("session", "token")

    receive_mail!(build_mail(from: "avery@example.test", subject: "Cannot download my receipt",
                             body: "The download button does nothing.", message_id: "<origin-1@example.test>"))
    @request = Request.sole
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  def acme = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")

  def avery = acme.users.find_by!(email: "avery@example.test")

  def reply_address = SupportAddress.reply_for(@request.reload)

  def reply_token = @request.reload.reply_token

  # A staff update through the API, as the staff app sends it.
  def staff_update(request_id, ticket, token: @agent_token)
    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{request_id}", params: { ticket: ticket }, headers: bearer(token), as: :json
    assert_response :ok, response.body
  end

  # What the customer sends back, from their mail client, to `to`.
  def customer_reply(to:, body: "It still fails.", from: "avery@example.test", message_id: nil)
    receive_mail!(build_mail(from: from, to: to, subject: "Re: Cannot download my receipt", body: body,
                             message_id: message_id))
  end

  # --- Staff replies going out ---------------------------------------------------

  test "a staff public reply is emailed to the requester" do
    staff_update(@request.id, comment: { body: "We fixed it. Try again." })

    mail = latest_mail("avery@example.test")
    assert_equal ["avery@example.test"], mail.to
    assert_equal ["support@example.test"], mail.from
    assert_equal "Re: Cannot download my receipt", mail.subject
    assert_includes mail.body.decoded, "We fixed it. Try again."
    assert_includes mail.body.decoded, "Hi Avery,"
  end

  test "the staff reply names the private reply address and threads to the opening email" do
    staff_update(@request.id, comment: { body: "Try again." })

    mail = latest_mail("avery@example.test")
    assert_equal ["reply+#{reply_token}@support.example.test"], mail.reply_to
    assert_equal "<origin-1@example.test>", mail["In-Reply-To"].to_s
    assert_equal "<origin-1@example.test>", mail["References"].to_s
  end

  test "a staff private note is not emailed" do
    staff_update(@request.id, comment: { body: "Checking with billing.", public: false })

    assert_empty mails_to("avery@example.test")
  end

  test "a status change alone is not emailed" do
    staff_update(@request.id, status: "solved")

    assert_empty mails_to("avery@example.test")
  end

  test "a reply on a request opened in the app is not emailed" do
    ben_token = customer_session(email: "ben@example.test", name: "Ben").dig("session", "token")
    opened = open_request!(ben_token)
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear

    staff_update(opened["id"], comment: { body: "On it." })

    assert_empty ActionMailer::Base.deliveries
  end

  test "the requester's own messages are not emailed back to them" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address)

    assert_empty mails_to("avery@example.test")
  end

  # --- The requester's replies coming back ---------------------------------------

  test "a reply to the reply address adds a public comment from the requester" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address, body: "It still fails on Safari.")

    comment = @request.comments.order(:id).last
    assert_equal "It still fails on Safari.", comment.body
    assert comment.public?
    assert_equal avery, comment.author
    assert_equal 1, Request.count, "a reply does not open another request"
  end

  test "a reply reopens a solved request" do
    staff_update(@request.id, status: "solved")

    customer_reply(to: reply_address)

    assert_equal "open", @request.reload.status
  end

  test "a reply reopens a pending request" do
    staff_update(@request.id, status: "pending")

    customer_reply(to: reply_address)

    assert_equal "open", @request.reload.status
  end

  test "a reply to an open request leaves it open" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address)

    assert_equal "open", @request.reload.status
  end

  test "a reply does not verify the requester" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address)

    refute avery.verified?
  end

  test "the reply address in a staff email returns the customer's answer to the same request" do
    staff_update(@request.id, comment: { body: "Did that work?" }, status: "solved")
    reply_to = latest_mail("avery@example.test").reply_to.first

    customer_reply(to: reply_to, body: "Yes, thanks!")

    assert_equal 1, Request.count
    assert_equal "open", @request.reload.status
    assert_equal "Yes, thanks!", @request.comments.order(:id).last.body
  end

  test "a reply with the same Message-ID is only recorded once" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address, message_id: "<answer-1@example.test>")
    customer_reply(to: reply_address, message_id: "<answer-1@example.test>")

    assert_equal 2, @request.comments.count, "the original message and one reply"
  end

  test "a reply sent to the reply address and the plain address is a reply, not a new request" do
    customer_reply(to: "#{reply_address}, acme@support.example.test")

    assert_equal 1, Request.count
    assert_equal 2, @request.comments.count
  end

  test "a plain message from the same customer opens a new request" do
    receive_mail!(build_mail(from: "avery@example.test", subject: "A different problem"))

    assert_equal 2, Request.count
    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
  end

  test "only the requester may reply by email" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address, from: "someone-else@example.test")

    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
    assert_equal "open", @request.reload.status
  end

  test "a reply from a staff member who is not the requester is refused" do
    customer_reply(to: reply_address, from: "sam@acme.test")

    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
  end

  test "a suspended requester cannot reply by email" do
    suspend_user!(token: @owner_token, user_id: avery.id)

    customer_reply(to: reply_address)

    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
  end

  test "a reply that names two different requests is refused" do
    receive_mail!(build_mail(from: "ben@example.test", subject: "Login", message_id: "<ben-1@example.test>"))
    other_reply = SupportAddress.reply_for(Request.find_by!(subject: "Login"))

    customer_reply(to: "#{reply_address}, #{other_reply}")

    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
    assert_equal 0, Request.find_by!(subject: "Login").comments.where(author: avery).count
  end

  test "a reply addressed to a second business is ignored" do
    signup!(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", email: "jo@globex.test")

    customer_reply(to: "#{reply_address}, globex@support.example.test")

    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
  end

  test "a reply whose request is gone is treated as a plain message" do
    customer_reply(to: "reply+#{'0' * 32}@support.example.test")

    assert_equal 1, @request.comments.count
    assert_equal 0, Request.where.not(id: @request.id).count, "an unknown reply address opens nothing"
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: Found a real bug. A single-part message with no `Content-Type` header has `mime_type == nil`, and RFC 2045 says that means plain text. My code only matched the literal `"text/plain"`, so such messages were silently treated as having no text. The fix is to treat a missing type as `text/plain` for lookup purposes. I'll also fix the brace issue in the test helper.

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - <<'EOF'
p = "app/models/mail_text.rb"
s = open(p).read()
old = """  def first_part(type)
    candidates = @mail.multipart? ? @mail.all_parts : [@mail]
    candidates.find { |part| part.mime_type == type && !part.attachment? }
  end
"""
new = """  def first_part(type)
    candidates = @mail.multipart? ? @mail.all_parts : [@mail]
    candidates.find { |part| part_type(part) == type && !part.attachment? }
  end

  # A part with no Content-Type is plain text, as RFC 2045 says.
  def part_type(part)
    part.mime_type || "text/plain"
  end
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
open(p, "w").write(s)

p = "test/models/automated_mail_test.rb"
s = open(p).read()
s = s.replace('automated?("', 'automated?({ "').replace('automated?(\n', 'automated?(\n')
import re
# Wrap hash-literal calls with braces: automated?({ "A" => "b" }) form
s = re.sub(r'automated\?\(\{ "([^"]+)" => ([^)]+?)\)$', lambda m: 'automated?({ "%s" => %s })' % (m.group(1), m.group(2)), s, flags=re.M)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print(s[s.find("test \"Auto"):s.find("test \"Auto")+200])
EOF

# Handles mail sent to a business's support address, or to a request's private reply address.
#
# Mail to the plain address opens a new request for the sender. If the sender is not yet a user
# of the business, they become a customer: unverified, and sent a verification link. Receiving
# mail never verifies anyone.
#
# Mail to a request's reply address is a reply on that request. Only its requester may send one.
#
# Mail that cannot be used is ignored: nothing is saved, nothing is sent back, and the Message-ID is
# left unclaimed, so a corrected retry with the same Message-ID is processed normally.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  # Stops processing with a reason. Nothing is sent to the sender.
  class Rejected < StandardError; end

  NO_SUBJECT = "(no subject)".freeze

  def process
    reject!("automated or list mail") if AutomatedMail.new(mail).automated?
    reject!("no sender address") if sender.empty?
    reject!("sent from the support domain") if sender.end_with?("@#{SupportAddress.domain}")
    reject!("no message text") if text.nil?
    reject!("already processed") if already_delivered?

    verification = deliver
    UserMailer.email_verification(*verification).deliver_later if verification
  rescue Rejected => error
    ignore!(error.message)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    ignore!(error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
  end

  private

  # Saves the request or reply, and claims the Message-ID, in one transaction. Returns [user, token]
  # when a new customer was created, so their verification link is sent only after the commit.
  #
  # The savepoint makes a rejection roll back everything the delivery wrote, even when this runs
  # inside an outer transaction.
  def deliver
    account, reply_token = target
    verification = nil

    Account.transaction(requires_new: true) do
      # Locking the business serializes deliveries with each other, with invitations and with
      # registrations, and makes the cancelled check current.
      account.lock!
      reject!("the business is cancelled") if account.cancelled?

      request = reply_token && account.requests.find_by(reply_token: reply_token)
      if request
        reply_to(request)
      else
        verification = open_request(account)
      end

      claim_message_id!
    end

    verification
  end

  # The business this message is for, and the reply token when it is a reply. Mail for no
  # business, or for more than one, is ignored. An unknown reply token is ignored too, so the
  # plain address still opens a new request.
  def target
    addresses = mail.recipients.filter_map { |address| SupportAddress.parse(address) }
    tokens = addresses.filter_map { |kind, value| value if kind == :reply }.uniq
    subdomains = addresses.filter_map { |kind, value| value if kind == :business }.uniq
    reject!("replies to more than one request") if tokens.many?

    reply_request = tokens.first && Request.find_by(reply_token: tokens.first)
    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: subdomains).to_a
    accounts |= [reply_request.account] if reply_request
    reject!("not addressed to a business") if accounts.empty?
    reject!("addressed to more than one business") if accounts.many?

    [accounts.first, reply_request&.reply_token]
  end

  # Only the requester may reply. Replies to pending or solved requests reopen them.
  def reply_to(request)
    requester = request.requester
    reject!("only the requester can reply by email") unless requester.email == sender
    reject!("the requester is suspended") if requester.suspended?

    request.requester_reply!(author: requester, body: body)
  end

  def open_request(account)
    requester, token = requester_for_sender(account)
    Request.open_from_email!(requester: requester, subject: subject, body: body, message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
    token && [requester, token]
  end

  # The existing user with the sender's address, or a new customer. A new customer is unverified
  # and gets a random password nobody knows. They verify through the emailed link, then choose a
  # password with a password reset.
  def requester_for_sender(account)
    existing = account.users.find_by(email: sender)
    if existing
      reject!("the sender is suspended") if existing.suspended?
      return [existing, nil]
    end

    # A pending invitation reserves the address, as it does for registration.
    reject!("the address has a pending invitation") if Invitation.pending_for_email?(account, sender)

    customer = account.users.create!(
      name: sender_name,
      email: sender,
      role: User::CUSTOMER,
      password: SecureRandom.hex(32)
    )
    [customer, UserToken.issue!(customer, :email_verification)]
  end

  # Marks the delivery processed. Two deliveries with one Message-ID can race here: the database
  # lets only one through, and the other rolls back everything it wrote.
  def claim_message_id!
    inbound_email.delivered!
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    reject!("already processed")
  end

  def already_delivered?
    ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.delivered
                               .where(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
                               .where.not(id: inbound_email.id)
                               .exists?
  end

  def ignore!(reason)
    logger.info("Inbound mail #{inbound_email.id} (#{inbound_email.message_id}) was not processed: #{reason}.")
    # Ends processing without sending a bounce message.
    bounced!
  end

  def reject!(reason)
    raise Rejected, reason
  end

  def sender
    @sender ||= Array(mail.from).first.to_s.strip.downcase
  end

  def sender_name
    name = clean_line(mail.from_address&.display_name)
    (name.presence || sender.split("@").first).truncate(User::NAME_MAX_LENGTH)
  end

  def subject
    clean_line(mail.subject).presence&.truncate(Request::SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH) || NO_SUBJECT
  end

  def body
    text.truncate(Comment::BODY_MAX_LENGTH)
  end

  def text
    @text ||= MailText.from(mail)
  end

  # A single line of text with no NUL characters or invalid UTF-8.
  def clean_line(value)
    value.to_s.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace).scrub("").delete("\u0000").squish
  end
end

### Receiving mail

The SMTP relay posts each message to `POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, with
`Content-Type: message/rfc822`, the raw message as the body, and HTTP basic auth: user
`actionmailbox`, password `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. A missing or wrong password gets `401`.
A message that was accepted gets `204`, including one that is then ignored. Processing happens
inside the request in test. In other environments it runs in the Active Job queue.

  two businesses is ignored. So is mail for an unknown or cancelled business.
- **A new request.** Mail to the plain address opens a new request. Its subject is the request's
  subject, and its plain-text body is the first comment. Attachments are left out. An HTML-only
  message is converted to text. A message with no subject gets the subject `(no subject)`.
  Bodies over 10,000 characters are cut to that length.
- **Customers.** A sender who is already a user of the business is reused, even if they are
  unverified. Otherwise a new customer is created with the sender's display name, and they are
  emailed a verification link. Receiving mail never verifies anyone. A new customer has no
  password. After verifying, they choose one with the password reset flow. Mail is refused when

the environment. Action Mailbox incinerates processed mail after 30 days.

module SupportAddress
  REPLY_LOCAL_PART = /\Areply\+(?<token>[0-9a-f]{32})\z/

  module_function

  def domain
    Helpdesk::Settings.support_domain
  end

  def for_account(account)
    "#{account.subdomain}@#{domain}"
  end

  def reply_for(request)
    "reply+#{request.reply_token}@#{domain}"
  end

  # Returns [:business, subdomain] or [:reply, token] for an address on the support domain, or nil
  # for anything else.
  def parse(address)
    address = Mail::Address.new(address.to_s).address
    local, host = address.to_s.downcase.split("@", 2)
    return unless host == domain

    if (match = REPLY_LOCAL_PART.match(local))
      [:reply, match[:token]]
    elsif local.match?(Account::SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT)
      [:business, local]
    end
  rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
    nil
  end

# The plain-text body of an email. This is the text/plain part when there is one, and otherwise
# the text/html part converted to text. Attachments are ignored.
class MailText
  NUL = "\u0000".freeze

  # Returns the body as UTF-8 text with Unix line endings, or nil when the message has no text.
  def self.from(mail)
    new(mail).body
  end

  def initialize(mail)
    @mail = mail
  end

  def body
    text = plain_text || html_text
    text && normalize(text).presence
  end

  private

  def plain_text
    first_part("text/plain")&.decoded
  end

  def html_text
    html = first_part("text/html")&.decoded
    html && html_to_text(html)
  end

  def first_part(type)
    candidates = @mail.multipart? ? @mail.all_parts : [@mail]
    candidates.find { |part| part_type(part) == type && !part.attachment? }
  end

  # A part with no Content-Type is plain text, as RFC 2045 says.
  def part_type(part)
    part.mime_type || "text/plain"
  end

  # Drops what a reader does not see, then turns the remaining markup into line breaks and text.
  def html_to_text(html)
    document = Nokogiri::HTML5(html)
    document.css("head, script, style").each(&:remove)
    document.css("br").each { |line_break| line_break.replace("\n") }
    document.css("p, div, li, tr, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6").each { |block| block.after("\n") }
    document.text
  end

  # Valid UTF-8 with Unix line endings. PostgreSQL cannot store NUL characters, so they go too.
  def normalize(text)
    text.to_s.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace).scrub("")
        .delete(NUL).gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
  end
end

results.content:
{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "## Email

Customers can email support from their mail client. Each business receives mail at
`SUBDOMAIN@HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`. For Acme, that is `acme@support.example.test`. Mail is
received through Action Mailbox's relay ingress.

### Receiving mail

The SMTP relay posts each message to `POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, with
`Content-Type: message/rfc822`, the raw message as the body, and HTTP basic auth: user
`actionmailbox`, password `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. A missing or wrong password gets `401`.
A message that was accepted gets `204`, including one that is then ignored. Processing happens
inside the request in test. In other environments it runs in the Active Job queue.

- **Which business.** The business comes from the To, Cc and Bcc recipients. Mail addressed to
  two businesses is ignored. So is mail for an unknown or cancelled business.
- **A new request.** Mail to the plain address opens a new request. Its subject is the request's
  subject, and its plain-text body is the first comment. Attachments are left out. An HTML-only
  message is converted to text. A message with no subject gets the subject `(no subject)`.
  Bodies over 10,000 characters are cut to that length.
- **Customers.** A sender who is already a user of the business is reused, even if they are
  unverified. Otherwise a new customer is created with the sender's display name, and they are
  emailed a verification link. Receiving mail never verifies anyone. A new customer has no
  password. After verifying, they choose one with the password reset flow. Mail is refused when
  the sender is suspended, or when their address has a pending invitation.
- **Replies.** Every request opened by email gets a private reply address,
  `reply+TOKEN@HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`. Mail to it is a reply on that request, and only the
  requester may send one. Any other sender is refused. A reply adds a public comment, and it reopens
  a `pending` or `solved` request. Mail to a request's reply address and the plain address is a
  reply, not a new request.
- **Duplicates.** A Message-ID that has already been processed is ignored, so a retried delivery
  does not open a second request.
- **Automated mail is ignored.** That covers `Auto-Submitted` (other than `no`), `Precedence:
  bulk`, `list` or `junk`, any `List-*` header, auto-responder headers, bounces (an empty return
  path), delivery reports, and senders such as `mailer-daemon` and `no-reply`. So does mail sent
  from the support domain itself.
- **Refused mail is not an error.** Mail that cannot be used is ignored: nothing is saved and
  nothing is sent back. That includes mail with no text or no usable sender. The Message-ID stays
  free, so a corrected or later delivery with the same Message-ID is processed normally.

Each raw message is kept as an Active Storage blob, so `config/storage.yml` must have a service for
the environment. Action Mailbox incinerates processed mail after 30 days.

### Sending replies

When staff post a public reply on a request opened by email, the reply is emailed to the
requester:

- From `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM`, to the requester's address, with the subject `Re:` followed by the
  request's subject.
- `Reply-To` is the request's private reply address, so the requester's next email comes back to the
  same request.
- `In-Reply-To` and `References` carry the Message-ID of the email that opened the request.

Private notes and status changes are not emailed. Neither are replies on requests opened in the
app, and the requester's own messages are never emailed back to them.

## Accounts and roles
"
}

steps.message:
Customers can now email `acme@support.example.test` and reply from their mail client, through Action Mailbox's relay ingress. The full suite passes: 404 runs, 0 failures. That's the 324 original tests plus 80 new ones, which go through the real relay endpoint with real RFC 822 messages.

## What it does

- **Relay:** `POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` with `message/rfc822` and basic auth (user `actionmailbox`, password `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`). A wrong password gets `401`. In test, mail is routed inside the request.
- **New tickets:** Mail to a business's plain address opens a request with the subject and the plain-text body. Business is found from To, Cc, and Bcc. Mail to two businesses is ignored.
- **Customers:** An existing user is reused. A new sender becomes an unverified customer with a verification email. Receiving mail never verifies anyone.
- **Replies out:** A staff public reply on an email-origin request is emailed to the requester. `Reply-To` is the request's private `reply+<token>@support.example.test` address, and threading headers point at the opening email.
- **Replies in:** Only the requester can reply through that address. A reply adds a public comment and reopens pending or solved requests.
- **Dedupe and retries:** Each Message-ID is processed at most once. Rejected mail is rolled back and its Message-ID stays free, so a corrected retry goes through. Automated and list mail is ignored.

## Decisions to review

- **Gem index replaced.** Action Mailbox's built-in unique index on `(message_id, message_checksum)` would have silently blocked retries of any failed delivery. I replaced it with a partial unique index that applies only to delivered rows.
- **Reply addresses are email-only.** Only email-origin requests get a reply address and outbound replies. Portal requests get neither.
- **Refused mail.** Mail with no text, no usable sender, or a suspended sender is dropped silently and gets `204`, as does any ignored mail. Subject-only mail is dropped rather than turned into a ticket.
- **New customers have no password.** They verify, then set one through the existing password-reset flow. The verification email text is shared and doesn't mention this.
- **Other choices:** Replies to ignored or rejected mail are never sent. Bodies over 10,000 characters are truncated. A sender who is already a staff member becomes the requester of their own ticket.

## Gaps before go-live

- **Spoofing.** Sender identity comes only from the `From` header, with no SPF or DKIM check. Anyone who can forge `From` can open tickets as a customer or reply as them. Check the relay's authentication results before relying on this.
- **Lost mail on restart.** Production uses the default `async` adapter, which the README already warns loses queued jobs. Inbound mail is now processed in that same adapter, and the relay has already been told `204`. Configure a persistent queue.
- **Portal omits support address.** Customers have no API field telling them their address. I didn't add one because the existing tenancy test pins the portal's exact JSON.
- **Storage.** Raw emails are kept on local disk in every environment. Use durable storage in production.

## Notes

- The database migrations are: the gem's Active Storage and Action Mailbox tables, the uniqueness change, and the request origin columns. They apply cleanly from scratch, and I checked the result against the dev database.
- `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD` must be set outside test. Without it the relay fails with a server error and accepts nothing.
- The README documents the new behavior. I also replaced its outdated "Replies do not send email yet."
